subject: Numeracy
title: Up, down, in front and behind
objectives: Children will follow instructions using up, down, in front and behind.
Children will describe where they are using one position word.
content: Understanding and using up, down, in front and behind in movement games, hide and find and obstacle courses.
teachingActivities: Say the position word as the child moves; use landmarks such as a chair or a tree; keep instructions to one at a time and then two.
learnerActivities: Move up and down, stand in front and behind objects and friends, follow instructions on an obstacle course and say where they are.
resources: A chair, a box and a soft toy
assessment: Check whether each child follows position instructions and says where an object or friend is.
expectedOutcomes: Moves to a position on request.
Says where an object is using one word.
crossCurricular: Social Habits: waiting and taking turns in a line

lessons.title: Up and down
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will move their bodies and objects up and down on request.
successCriteria: Raises and lowers an object when asked
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use in, on and under and follow simple one-step instructions in games.
lessons.starter: Raise your arms and say "Up!" Lower them and say "Down!" Hold a scarf high and let it float down. Say "Down it comes."
teacherActivities: Do the actions: arms up, arms down, stand up, sit down. Say the words as you move.
Hold a ball high and say "Up". Lower it and say "Down". Let children try.
Let each child step up onto a low bench with help and step down.
Play "Up and down" with a scarf: toss it up and watch it float down.
learnerActivities: Children copy the actions and say "up" and "down".
Children raise and lower the ball when asked.
Child steps up and down, saying the words.
Children toss the scarf up and say "down" as it lands.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Do the actions: arms up, arms down, stand up, sit down. Say the words as you move. Children: Children copy the actions and say "up" and "down".
Step 2. Teacher: Hold a ball high and say "Up". Lower it and say "Down". Let children try. Children: Children raise and lower the ball when asked.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child step up onto a low bench with help and step down. Children: Child steps up and down, saying the words.
Step 4. Teacher: Play "Up and down" with a scarf: toss it up and watch it float down. Children: Children toss the scarf up and say "down" as it lands.

practical.title: Up and down game
steps: Call up or down and children move their bodies or objects.
Change the speed of the calls.
practical.safety: Use a low, stable bench with an adult beside each child; keep the floor clear; no jumping from the bench.

differentiation.support: Move together with an adult and use one word at a time.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to give "up" and "down" instructions to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you put your hands up?
Where is the ball now?
questions.expected: Up or down, depending on where it is.

lessons.conclusion: Lower arms slowly and say "Down, down, sit down."
lessons.homeConnection: Play "up and down" with a toy or a scarf at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "move their bodies and objects up and down on request" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Up, up, up, we stretch so high. Down, down, down, we sit on the ground.

lessons.title: In front and behind
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will stand in front of and behind a chair or a friend when asked.
successCriteria: Moves in front of or behind an object
Says in front or behind with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use in, on and under and follow simple one-step instructions in games.
lessons.starter: Put a soft toy on the floor in front of a chair and say "Teddy is in front of the chair." Move it behind and say "Teddy is behind the chair."
teacherActivities: Stand in front of the chair and say "I am in front." Walk behind it and say "I am behind."
Ask each child to stand in front of the chair, then behind it.
Place the soft toy in front, behind and say "Where is Teddy?"
Line up in a queue and say "Who is in front? Who is behind?"
learnerActivities: Children watch and copy the movements.
Child moves as instructed.
Children say "in front" or "behind".
Children point to the child in front or behind them.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Stand in front of the chair and say "I am in front." Walk behind it and say "I am behind." Children: Children watch and copy the movements.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask each child to stand in front of the chair, then behind it. Children: Child moves as instructed.
Step 3. Teacher: Place the soft toy in front, behind and say "Where is Teddy?" Children: Children say "in front" or "behind".
Step 4. Teacher: Line up in a queue and say "Who is in front? Who is behind?" Children: Children point to the child in front or behind them.

practical.title: Chair game
steps: Place a chair in the middle.
Children take turns to stand in front of or behind it.
practical.safety: Use a stable chair; children walk calmly; keep the area clear.

differentiation.support: Use a large object and an adult to guide the movement.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to put two toys in front and behind and describe.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you go behind the chair?

lessons.conclusion: Queue up and say "Who is in front?" before moving to the next activity.
lessons.homeConnection: Use in front and behind when lining up shoes or toys.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "stand in front of and behind a chair or a friend when asked" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

pictures: A toy in front of and behind a chair

lessons.title: Obstacle course words
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will follow position instructions on a simple obstacle course.
successCriteria: Completes the course following the instructions
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use in, on and under and follow simple one-step instructions in games.
resources: A tunnel, a low bench, cones, a mat
lessons.starter: Show the obstacle course. Say "Today we crawl through the tunnel, walk around the cone and step up on the bench."
teacherActivities: Walk the course once yourself and say each position word: "through", "around", "up", "down".
Let each child try the course with an adult walking beside them.
Ask the child to say what they are doing: "I am going up."
Change the course by moving a cone in front or behind and ask "Where is the cone?"
learnerActivities: Children watch and say the words.
Child follows the course and hears the words.
Child says a position word.
Children say where the cone is.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Walk the course once yourself and say each position word: "through", "around", "up", "down". Children: Children watch and say the words.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child try the course with an adult walking beside them. Children: Child follows the course and hears the words.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask the child to say what they are doing: "I am going up." Children: Child says a position word.
Step 4. Teacher: Change the course by moving a cone in front or behind and ask "Where is the cone?" Children: Children say where the cone is.

practical.title: Position course
steps: Set up a tunnel, cones and a bench in a line.
Each child goes through the course.
practical.safety: Use low, stable equipment; crawl only; an adult stays at each obstacle; no running.

differentiation.support: Take one obstacle at a time with an adult.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to design and explain a course for a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Where did you go?
questions.expected: Through the tunnel, up the bench.

questions.question: Is the cone in front or behind you?

expectedOutcomes: Follows position instructions on a course
lessons.conclusion: Walk the course slowly together one more time and say each word.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a small obstacle course with cushions and a chair at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "follow position instructions on a simple obstacle course" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Follow the leader positions
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will give and follow position instructions in a game.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use in, on and under and follow simple one-step instructions in games.
lessons.starter: Say "Let us play follow the leader! I say where to go and you do it." Stand behind the chair and call "Behind!"
teacherActivities: Call an instruction: "Stand behind the chair." "Put the toy in front of the box."
Choose a leader. Let the leader call "Up" or "Down" or "In front".
Change leaders every minute so everyone has a turn.
Finish with a calm game: "Sit down, stand up, sit down."
learnerActivities: Children follow the instruction.
Leader calls an instruction and the group follows.
Each child leads one instruction.
Children follow the slow instructions.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Call an instruction: "Stand behind the chair." "Put the toy in front of the box." Children: Children follow the instruction.
Step 2. Teacher: Choose a leader. Let the leader call "Up" or "Down" or "In front". Children: Leader calls an instruction and the group follows.
Step 3. Teacher: Change leaders every minute so everyone has a turn. Children: Each child leads one instruction.
Step 4. Teacher: Finish with a calm game: "Sit down, stand up, sit down." Children: Children follow the slow instructions.

practical.title: Position follow the leader
steps: The leader gives one instruction at a time.
practical.safety: Give children space; keep movements gentle; stop if the game becomes too boisterous.

differentiation.support: Pair the child with an adult leader and use one word.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to give two instructions in a row.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Where is the toy?
questions.expected: In front of or behind something.

lessons.conclusion: Slow the game down and finish with "Sit down together."
lessons.homeConnection: Play follow the leader at home using up, down, in front and behind.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "give and follow position instructions in a game" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Position stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show they understand up, down, in front and behind at three stations.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use in, on and under and follow simple one-step instructions in games.
resources: Station 1: up and down with scarves
lessons.starter: Sing the position song and show the three stations.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
Ask "Put the toy in front of the chair" and "Go up the bench."
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children play at each station.
Child follows the instruction.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children play at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Put the toy in front of the chair" and "Go up the bench." Children: Child follows the instruction.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Use low equipment; supervise each station; keep the floor clear.

differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to run the obstacle course game for a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: follows up and down instructions; follows in front and behind instructions; says where an object is.

questions.question: Where is Teddy?
questions.expected: In front or behind the chair.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 4
Uses position words with growing accuracy
lessons.conclusion: Sing the position song and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Use position words in talk at home this week.
